## Summary

Records the ethos mission audit trail behind PR #215, and corrects two beads that asserted things which were not true.

## Mission trail

| Mission | Work | Rounds |
|---|---|---|
| `m-2026-09-06-001` | Restore the provenance job | 2 |
| `m-2026-09-06-002` | Tag ref instead of SHA, after Bugbot's finding | 2 |
| `m-2026-09-06-003` | Quote the local-make rule verbatim | 1 |
| `m-2026-09-06-004` | Document the publish-before-provenance gap | 2 |

All four: worker `jdc`, evaluator `gjm`, leader `claude`.

## Bead corrections

- **`xboing-7z8x`** — closed, and its own description corrected. It claimed every release since 2026-08-30 shipped unattested. It did not: `v1.0.11` was cut 71 minutes *before* PR #209 merged, and no tag has been cut since. The gap was latent, not active. I wrote that overstatement when filing the bead this morning; this fixes it.
- **`xboing-qlw7`** — annotated. Its close reason asserts SLSA L3 provenance shipped in PR #209. It did not — #209 merged into a stacked base that never reached master. The bead stays closed; the note records that the claim was false and the check that detects the pattern: `git merge-base --is-ancestor <merge-sha> master`.
- **`xboing-gqhx`** — new. Make the tag release atomic so a failed attestation cannot leave a public unattested Release.

## A gap in the trail, stated rather than hidden

Missions 001–003 have no `log.jsonl`. Ethos emitted `no session in context -- active-mission sidecar not updated` on every mission create in this session and wrote no event log for those three; only 004 produced one. Contracts, reflections and results — the substance of the trail — are complete for all four. Flagging it so the absence isn't later read as tampering.

Lock files (`.lock`, `.create.lock`) are runtime artifacts and remain untracked, consistent with the existing missions in that directory.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green (this changes no code — YAML/JSONL artifacts and bead state only)

Not included: four modified `.claude/agents/*.md` files in the working tree. That's pre-existing ethos regeneration drift (the "reports to" line changed from Claude Agento to Justin C. Kibell), unrelated to this work, and left for a maintainer decision.

## Summary

Commits the four `.claude/agents/*.md` files that ethos regenerates from the team collaboration graph — they had been drifting uncommitted all session — and records the current `ethos doctor` state.

## Agent files: a reporting-hierarchy change, not just formatting

| File | Reporting line |
|---|---|
| `gjm`, `jdc`, `sjl` | Claude Agento (COO/VP Engineering) → **Justin C. Kibell (jck)** |
| `jck` | Claude Agento (COO/VP Engineering) → **Claude Agento (claude)** |

So the structure becomes `claude → jck → {gjm, jdc, sjl}` — the original author as domain lead over the three implementers. Previously all four reported directly to the COO.

That matches how the repo already works: `CLAUDE.md` requires jck approval for gameplay-affecting changes, so routing the implementers through him reflects the actual gate. Plus cosmetic quoting of `skills: "baseline-ops"` in all four.

No tool grants, model choices, or hook configs change **in this diff**.

## Correction — and it surfaced a real inconsistency

An earlier version of this description claimed *"jck stays read-only (Read/Grep/Glob/WebFetch)"*. **That was false, and Copilot caught it.** `jck.md` grants `Read`, **`Write`**, **`Edit`**, `Grep`, `Glob`, `WebFetch`. Those grants are pre-existing and untouched by this PR — but the claim was wrong, and chasing it found a genuine repo defect:

`.claude/rules/delegation.md:59` states verbatim:

> `jck` is read-only (Read/Grep/Glob/WebFetch). Never `implement`/`test`.

That is **not true of the actual agent config**, and hasn't been for some time. The governance rule and the enforced permissions disagree.

There's a subtlety worth preserving. Bead `xboing-c-xzt` (open since 2026-05-02) proposes extending jck with **Write + Bash** so research/design missions can self-file. Checking the current config:

| Grant | State |
|---|---|
| `Write` / `Edit` | **Present** — so `delegation.md` is wrong |
| `Bash` | **Absent** — so the bead's actual motivation still stands |

jck still cannot run `ethos mission result`, which needs Bash. So that bead is *partially* addressed, not stale — and its description now misstates the premise by calling jck read-only.

Recorded on `xboing-c-xzt` rather than fixed here: changing a governance rule and a permission grant deserves its own deliberate change, not a drive-by edit in a metadata PR.

## `ethos doctor` — it exits 1

`CLAUDE.md` Session Start step 4 says it "must report all PASS." It does not, and hasn't been passing.

```
  Identity directory       PASS  <repo>/.punt-labs/ethos/identities
  Human identity           PASS  Jim Freeman (jfreeman)
  Default agent            PASS  claude
  Duplicate fields         PASS  no duplicates
  Orphaned agent files     FAIL  orphaned agent files (not on any team): latex-tech-architect
  Audit seal hook          PASS  not enabled here
  Seal hook currency       PASS  no Seal hook section installed
  Trailer hook currency    PASS  no Trailer hook section installed
  Repo-only completeness   PASS  resolution: layered — not applicable
  Local extension files    WARN  no .gitignore rule for .punt-labs/**/*.local.* — add it before running `ethos ext set --local`
  Extension key names      PASS  no credential-named keys
  Mission file hand-edits  PASS  no hand-edited mission files
```

Filed as **`xboing-icp1`** with full detail. Two notes on resolution:

- **`latex-tech-architect` is tracked and works** — it appears in the session's available agent types. It's simply absent from the team config. The fix is almost certainly to *add it to a team*, not delete it; removing a functioning agent to silence a doctor line would be the wrong resolution. Left for a decision rather than guessed at.
- The WARN is harmless today (no `.local.*` files exist) but becomes real exposure the moment anyone runs `ethos ext set --local` — which is what it's pre-empting.

## The finding doctor does *not* flag as a problem

```
Trailer hook currency    PASS  no Trailer hook section installed
```

That check validates **currency**, not **presence**. So this repo — whose `docs/GIT.md` states *"a code commit with no mission trailer means the work skipped the mission process — that is a defect"* — gets a **green line** for having no trailer hook at all. Same for `Seal hook currency`.

## This materially simplifies `xboing-yeuw`

`ethos enable --help`:

> "…chains the audit-seal and **trailer git hooks**. Idempotent — re-running is the upgrade path."

The repo was enabled before that feature existed and `enable` hasn't been re-run. So part 3 of that bead is **one command**, not the design exercise my earlier analysis implied. "Chains" also confirms ethos coexists with beads' hooks rather than fighting over the single-valued `core.hooksPath`.

**Part 2 is untouched by this.** The session sidecar still isn't written (133 session dirs, one `active-mission` file, stale since Sept 2), so the hook may install and stamp *empty* trailers. The bead says to verify with a real commit under a real mission afterwards rather than assuming the install fixed it — assuming is exactly the failure that bead documents.

## A pattern, stated plainly

Five distinct instances this session of a control or claim reading as true while being false: SLSA provenance documented as present while absent; a SHA-pinned generator running green and emitting nothing; `make lint` asserting CI parity on a different linter version; a doctor check that can't distinguish "current" from "absent"; and now a governance rule asserting a permission boundary the config doesn't enforce.

Every one was falsifiable in a single command. The code in these PRs was verified by running it and was largely correct. The prose describing it was not verified at all until a reviewer pushed back.
